one_liner: Competes in a sport for a living - through a league, a federation, or a sports quota job.
job_roles: Cricketer | Footballer | Athletics Competitor | Wrestler | Boxer | Badminton Player | Kabaddi Player | Shooter | Hockey Player | Chess Player | Para-Athlete | Motorsport Racer | Rally Co-Driver
entrance_exams: Sports quota recruitment (Railways, police, banks, PSUs) | Franchise league drafts
self_emp_route: Prize money, appearance fees, coaching and endorsements - and for most athletes outside the three league sports, none of these is the main income. The sports quota government post is.
ai_reason: Among the least exposed professions in the dataset. Sport is a human body competing against another human body and an audience that wants to watch people do it. Nothing generative touches the work. Chess Player is the one genuine exception in a sense no other profession faces: engines have been superhuman for decades, and the game survived because the market was never for the best moves but for people playing.
role_spread: [Chess Player, Shooter] higher: attention_span, reasoning, conscientiousness / lower: bodily || [Cricketer, Footballer, Kabaddi Player] higher: extraversion, confidence, bodily / lower: neuroticism || [Para-Athlete] higher: neuroticism, conscientiousness, existential / lower: extraversion || [Motorsport Racer, Rally Co-Driver] higher: spatial, confidence, attention_span / lower: neuroticism
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. Serious training starts in childhood; by class 11 an athlete is usually already competing at state level. -> training: Academy, SAI centre, Khelo India centre or a private club. Selection is by performance at district and state meets. -> competition: Place in National Championships, National Games or Category A/B/C championships - this is what unlocks both selection and the sports quota. -> work: A league contract in cricket, football or kabaddi; or - far more commonly - a sports quota post in the railways, police, a bank or the armed forces.
review_reason: Two gaps. First, this is a power-law income like Actor and Digital Content Creator, and a range misrepresents it. Second and more fixable: the sports quota route is the realistic outcome for most athletes and the record has no sourced figure for what a Level 1 to Level 5 railway post actually pays in hand. That number exists - it is on the 7th CPC matrix - and until it is fetched the most likely outcome of this career is unquantified. A third gap has been added: motorsport is PAY-TO-RACE and this record's cost_of_entry_lakh of 3.0 does not describe it at all. A sourced figure for an Indian karting or formula season is needed, and if it is as far outside the range as expected, Motorsport Racer may need to leave this record for one of its own.
nuances: [economics] The single most misunderstood record in this sector. Outside cricket, football and kabaddi, an Indian athlete's income is usually not from sport at all - it is a 7th CPC government salary obtained THROUGH sport via the sports quota, at Level 1 to Level 5. That is a modest but permanent, pensionable job, and it is a far better outcome than the word 'athlete' suggests to most families. || [entry_window] There is a real and brutal window that this schema field cannot hold, because it is not about age. Sports quota eligibility counts achievements from the current and previous two financial years only. An athlete who peaks at 19 and declines by 23 can be shut out of the route entirely, having given the years. || [demand_signal] Low, and it should be read as 'very few paid places' rather than 'do not do this'. Sport at school and state level is participation; the number of people paid to compete in India is small in every discipline except cricket. || [economics] economics.distribution is 'power_law', which is a statement that the range and the midpoint should not be read as a typical income. Outside cricket, football and kabaddi almost nobody earns from competing. The realistic outcome is a sports quota government salary, which is a different distribution entirely. The compensation filter does not fire on a power_law record, because deleting a profession on the strength of a number the record itself calls meaningless would be worse than showing it. || [economics] MOTORSPORT IS PAY-TO-RACE AND THE COST FIGURE ON THIS RECORD DOES NOT COVER IT. Every other athlete here has a cost of entry near 3 lakh and earns from competing. A motorsport racer BUYS THE SEAT - karting through to formula and touring car seasons are funded by the driver or by sponsorship the driver must raise themselves, and a season runs to many lakh. The income structure is inverted relative to the rest of the profession, and a family should understand that before a teenager asks for the first karting season. No sourced Indian figure for a season's cost was found, which is why it is stated as a shape rather than a number.

one_liner: Trains athletes and teams to perform - technique, tactics, conditioning and selection.
job_roles: Sports Coach | Grassroots & Youth Coach | Academy Coach | Strength & Conditioning Coach | Talent Scout | Team Analyst | Goalkeeping & Specialist Skills Coach | Rehabilitation & Return-to-Play Coach
entrance_exams: NSNIS Patiala coaching diploma | Sports quota recruitment (Railways, police, banks, PSUs) | Federation coaching licences (AIFF, BCCI and others)
self_emp_route: Private coaching, running an academy, or personal coaching of individual athletes. An academy with fifty paying children earns more reliably than most salaried coaching posts.
ai_reason: Low exposure. Coaching is watching a specific body move, knowing what is wrong, and getting a person to change a habit under pressure - none of which is a text problem. Team Analyst is the exposed role: video tagging and statistical breakdown is already largely automated, and what survives is the interpretation. Grassroots & Youth Coach is the safest work here and also the largest employer.
role_spread: [Strength & Conditioning Coach, Rehabilitation & Return-to-Play Coach] higher: logical, reasoning, conscientiousness / lower: extraversion || [Talent Scout] higher: attention_span, long_term_memory, reasoning / lower: agreeableness || [Grassroots & Youth Coach] higher: agreeableness, emotional_intelligence, extraversion / lower: neuroticism
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. Most coaches come from having played the sport. -> training: NSNIS Patiala diploma or certificate in sports coaching, a federation coaching licence, or a BPEd/MPEd. None is legally required. -> licence: Sport-specific federation licences - AIFF and BCCI run graded levels. These are what clubs and academies actually ask for. -> work: Academy, school, club, state association or SAI centre; or private coaching on your own account.
nuances: [professional_sector] A genuinely arguable placement. DECISIONS.md 2 sends teaching-anything to Sector 12, and a coach clearly teaches. It sits here because the object of concern is COMPETITIVE PERFORMANCE rather than learning: a coach is accountable for whether the athlete wins, selects the squad, and manages injury and load. A Physical Education Teacher, who is accountable for a curriculum and a class, is routed to Sector 12 instead. || [licensing_body] Null, and worth stating plainly because the National Sports Governance Act 2025 has just created new statutory machinery. That Act regulates federations, tribunals and elections - it licenses no coach. Federation coaching licences are real gates but they are contractual, set by employers and competitions.

one_liner: Gets ordinary people fitter and keeps them safe doing it - gyms, studios, homes, online.
job_roles: Personal Trainer | Gym Instructor | Group Fitness Instructor | Aerobics & Dance Fitness Instructor | Functional Training Coach | Aqua Fitness Instructor | Online Fitness Coach | Senior & Special Population Trainer
entrance_exams: Personal training certifications (SPEFL-SC, ACE, ACSM and others)
self_emp_route: Personal training clients taken directly, a small studio, or online coaching. Trainers with a full private roster earn multiples of the gym floor salary, which is why almost everyone in this profession is trying to get there.
ai_reason: Low exposure with one clear crack. Online Fitness Coach is directly exposed - generating a training programme from goals, height and weight is exactly what a model does well, and app based coaching already competes on price. What survives is presence: spotting a failing squat, adjusting a grip, and being the reason someone turned up at six in the morning. Personal Trainer and Senior & Special Population Trainer are protected by touch and liability.
role_spread: [Online Fitness Coach] higher: verbal, conscientiousness, logical / lower: bodily || [Senior & Special Population Trainer] higher: agreeableness, emotional_intelligence, attention_span / lower: confidence || [Group Fitness Instructor, Aerobics & Dance Fitness Instructor] higher: extraversion, musical, confidence / lower: attention_span
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream, or none. Most certifying bodies require class 12 or equivalent. -> certification: A personal training certification - SPEFL-SC / NSQF aligned, or an international body. Gyms ask for one; no law does. -> work: Gym floor instructor, then personal training clients. Almost all Indian gym trainers start salaried and move to commission. -> independence: Own client roster, a studio, or online coaching - where the income actually changes.
nuances: [demand_signal] High and genuinely growing - urban gym membership, corporate wellness and post-pandemic health awareness have all expanded the market. This is the most reliably employable profession in Sector 11 and the one with the lowest barrier to entry, which also means the most competition. || [licensing_body] Null, and this is a real consumer-safety gap rather than a neutral fact. Anyone in India may call themselves a personal trainer and take money to load a stranger's spine. Certification is entirely a private market with no floor.

one_liner: Runs the competition itself - refereeing, umpiring, judging, timing and scoring.
job_roles: Referee | Umpire | Match Official | Technical Official | Judge (Scored Sports) | Timekeeper & Scorer | Match Commissioner | Anti-Doping Chaperone
entrance_exams: Federation officiating examinations (BCCI, AIFF and others)
self_emp_route: Match fees, which is how essentially all officiating is paid. Officials at the top of a national panel in cricket earn a real income; everyone below that is doing it alongside another job.
ai_reason: Genuinely contested, and this is the one profession in Sector 11 where technology has already taken work. Timekeeper & Scorer is substantially automated, and ball tracking, goal-line technology and video review have moved decisions away from the on-field official in every sport that can afford them. What remains is the part machines cannot do: managing twenty-two angry people, applying judgment where the code is silent, and being the person accountable for the call.
role_spread: [Judge (Scored Sports)] higher: attention_span, conscientiousness, spatial / lower: extraversion || [Referee, Umpire] higher: confidence, neuroticism, bodily / lower: agreeableness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> certification: State or national federation officiating examination for the sport - BCCI's umpiring levels, AIFF referee courses and their equivalents. -> panel: Get onto a district, then state, then national panel. Progression is by assessment on matches actually officiated. -> work: Match fees per fixture. Only the top national panels in cricket offer anything resembling a full income.
review_reason: No sourced figure for Indian match fees at any level, in any sport, and match fees are the entire income of this profession. At 4.9 LPA mid-career with a named self-employment route and no ceiling, the record cannot distinguish a weekend district official from a national panel umpire - which is the only distinction that matters here.
nuances: [economics] Match-fee income, and for almost everyone in this profession it is a second income rather than a livelihood. The wide mid-career range is the gap between a district panel official officiating on weekends and a national panel cricket umpire. || [demand_signal] Low in paid terms and steady in real terms - every competition needs officials and India is chronically short of qualified ones, particularly in women's sport and outside cricket. Scarcity here has not translated into pay.

one_liner: Takes people safely into mountains, rivers and the sea, and teaches them to move there.
job_roles: Mountaineering Instructor | Trekking Guide | Rock Climbing Instructor | White Water Rafting Guide | Scuba Diving Instructor | Ski Instructor | Paragliding Instructor | Outdoor Education Facilitator | Wilderness First Responder
entrance_exams: Mountaineering course admission (NIM, HMI and state institutes) | Scuba and paragliding certifications (PADI, SSI and equivalents)
self_emp_route: Running your own trips, or a small operation with equipment. Owning gear - boats, ropes, dive kit - is what separates a guide on a day rate from an operator taking the margin.
ai_reason: Essentially unexposed, and one of the clearest cases in the model of physical skill in an unstructured environment being a moat rather than a liability. Route-finding, reading weather, judging whether a client can continue and rescuing them when they cannot are all decisions made with a body in a place. No role here has meaningful exposure.
role_spread: [Outdoor Education Facilitator] higher: agreeableness, emotional_intelligence, verbal / lower: bodily || [Scuba Diving Instructor, Paragliding Instructor] higher: conscientiousness, logical, attention_span / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> certification: Basic and Advanced Mountaineering courses at NIM Uttarkashi, HMI Darjeeling or another government institute; or international certification for diving and paragliding. -> experience: Logged days - summits, dives, river descents or flights. This is what actually qualifies you in the eyes of an employer. -> work: Adventure tour operators, outdoor education companies, or your own operation. Work is seasonal and tied to a specific geography.
nuances: [demand_signal] Moderate and concentrated - this work exists in Uttarakhand, Himachal, Ladakh, the Northeast, Goa and the Andamans and almost nowhere else. It is also strongly seasonal, so a full year's income usually means following the season across two regions or holding a winter job. || [professional_sector] Placed here rather than in Sector 16 with travel because the object of concern is physical performance and safety in a demanding environment, not hospitality. Adventure tourism is the EMPLOYER, and DECISIONS.md 2.2 says an employer is a tag.

one_liner: Competes or works professionally in organised competitive video gaming.
job_roles: Professional Player | Esports Coach | Team Analyst (Esports) | Shoutcaster | Tournament Administrator | Esports Team Manager | Observer & Production Operator
self_emp_route: Streaming and content alongside competing, which is how most Indian esports players actually earn. Prize money alone supports very few.
ai_reason: The most exposed profession in Sector 11 and the reason is unusual: the competitive titles themselves are AI-adjacent, and the surrounding jobs are digital. Team Analyst (Esports) is directly exposed - match review and draft analysis is pattern recognition over recorded data. Professional Player is protected in the same way Chess Player is: the audience is watching humans compete, and superhuman bots have existed in several titles for years without affecting that at all.
role_spread: [Shoutcaster, Observer & Production Operator] higher: verbal, extraversion, short_term_memory / lower: neuroticism || [Esports Coach, Team Analyst (Esports)] higher: reasoning, logical, attention_span / lower: confidence
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. -> ranking: Reach the top competitive ranks of a title with an Indian scene. This is public and verifiable, which makes entry unusually meritocratic. -> team: Join an organised roster and compete in qualifiers and tournaments. -> work: Team salary and prize money, streaming income, or the non-playing roles - coaching, casting, tournament operations.
review_reason: Aspiration-to-reality gap is the widest in the dataset. No sourced figure exists for Indian esports salaries, prize distribution or the number of paid roster spots, and every one of those is needed before this record can be shown to a fifteen-year-old. Decide also whether the very short playing career should be surfaced as a structural warning rather than left in a nuance.
nuances: [demand_signal] Low, and this needs saying bluntly because it is one of the most aspired-to careers among Indian teenagers. India has a very large gaming AUDIENCE and a very small number of paid competitive places - perhaps a few hundred salaried players nationally across all titles. Reading audience size as opportunity is the DECISIONS.md 8.45 error in its most tempting form. || [economics] A power-law distribution again, and with a shorter career than any other profession in this dataset - competitive playing careers commonly end in the mid-twenties. The non-playing roles are the realistic long-term work and they pay less than the equivalent job outside esports. || [years_to_qualify] Two years is the time to reach a competitive roster, not a qualification - there is none. What the number hides is that the training is thousands of hours of play with no transferable credential at the end if it does not work out. || [economics] economics.distribution is 'power_law', which is a statement that the range and the midpoint should not be read as a typical income. A few hundred paid roster places nationally against a very large amateur population, and a playing career that commonly ends in the mid-twenties. The compensation filter does not fire on a power_law record, because deleting a profession on the strength of a number the record itself calls meaningless would be worse than showing it.

one_liner: Measures what athletes do and turns it into training decisions - physiology, biomechanics, data.
job_roles: Sports Scientist | Exercise Physiologist | Biomechanist | Performance Analyst | Sports Data Analyst | Athlete Monitoring Specialist | Sports Psychologist (Performance) | Talent Identification Analyst
self_emp_route: Consultancy to clubs, academies and individual athletes, usually after building a reputation inside an institution. A small private testing or analysis practice is the common form.
ai_reason: The most exposed non-esports role here. Performance Analyst and Sports Data Analyst work is video tagging, event coding and statistical modelling, and automated tracking already does most of the collection - what survives is deciding what the numbers mean for one athlete's next eight weeks. Exercise Physiologist and Biomechanist are protected by having to put sensors on a real body and interpret an individual's response.
role_spread: [Sports Psychologist (Performance)] higher: emotional_intelligence, verbal, agreeableness / lower: logical || [Sports Data Analyst, Performance Analyst] higher: logical, spatial, attention_span / lower: extraversion
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream; Biology and Physical Education help for the physiology route. -> degree: BSc/MSc in Sports Science, Exercise Physiology, or a BPEd/MPEd. Data-side entrants often come from statistics or computing. -> work: SAI centre, national federation, a professional club, or a private high-performance facility. -> specialisation: Physiology, biomechanics, analysis or psychology - they diverge quickly and only analysis transfers easily outside sport.
nuances: [demand_signal] Low in India specifically, and the reason is structural: high performance support staff exist where there is money in the sport, which in India means cricket, a handful of federations and the SAI system. The skills transfer well abroad and to general healthcare, which is why pathway is 'any'. || [industrial_sectors] Tagged to EXT-RND as well as SPEFL because a good deal of this work is genuine applied research. The boundary with Sector 3 is method: a sports scientist measuring an athlete to change their training is intervening, not investigating.

one_liner: Prepares and maintains where sport is played - pitches, courts, pools, tracks and gyms.
job_roles: Groundsman | Pitch Curator | Turf Technician | Sports Facility Maintenance Technician | Swimming Pool Technician | Equipment & Kit Manager | Gym Floor Technician | Court & Track Maintenance Worker
self_emp_route: Contract maintenance of grounds and facilities for schools, clubs and housing societies - a small crew and equipment is the whole business, and it is how experienced ground staff raise their income.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed. Preparing a surface is outdoor physical work responding to weather, soil and use, and there is no digital output to substitute for. The one role with any exposure is Equipment & Kit Manager, through inventory software rather than through anything interesting.
role_spread: [Pitch Curator] higher: naturalistic, long_term_memory, reasoning / lower: extraversion || [Equipment & Kit Manager] higher: conscientiousness, attention_span / lower: bodily
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. -> training: On the job under a working groundsman. Turf management courses exist and are rare; almost nobody enters through one. -> work: Ground staff at a club, stadium, school, university or municipal facility. -> specialisation: Curation, turf science or facility management - the routes by which this becomes a skilled trade rather than manual work.
review_reason: No sourced wage figure for Indian ground staff or curators, and no figure for what a contract maintenance operation earns - the route named as the way out of a 4.2 LPA employed ceiling. Also unresolved: whether the senior cricket curator role is sufficiently different in pay and standing to need its own treatment.
nuances: [economics] The base layer of the sports sector, and it fails the compensation filter. Ground staff at most Indian clubs and municipal facilities are on casual or contract terms. The exception worth knowing is that a recognised cricket pitch curator at a first class venue is a genuinely skilled and respected position. || [demand_signal] Moderate and quietly stable - every school, club, stadium, university and gated community with a sports facility needs this work done, and the number of such facilities is growing. It is one of the few sports livelihoods available in a small town.
